scope: Incremental discovery screen and selected abstract/official-source appraisal, not a systematic review. Clinical review: primary PubMed abstracts; full text and supplements not independently appraised. Older profile dates retained unless new clinical findings added.

retatrutide.findings: November 8, 2026: TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA reported knee-osteoarthritis outcomes in 445 and 574 randomized adults without diabetes, respectively. Retatrutide reduced pain scores and body weight more than placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, intention-to-treat differences in WOMAC pain versus placebo were −1.70 and −1.38 points for the two studied groups. Eli Lilly funded the trials.
retatrutide.limits: TRIUMPH-1-OA is a substudy of the parent trial, not an independent replication. Pain improvement does not establish cartilage regeneration or separate direct joint effects from weight-related effects. Pain estimates differ between the reported hybrid and intention-to-treat analyses.
retatrutide.safety: The osteoarthritis report described more serious adverse events with retatrutide than placebo; gastrointestinal events were the most common adverse events. These results do not establish general safety.

survodutide.findings: November 9, 2026: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT randomized 5,530 adults with obesity and increased cardiovascular risk; 5,507 received treatment. Over a median 22 months, the primary cardiovascular composite hazard ratio was 0.89 (95% CI 0.67–1.18) versus placebo. This met the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.65. Boehringer Ingelheim funded the study.
survodutide.limits: Noninferiority under the specified margin is not proof of cardiovascular superiority. The confidence interval includes no difference and possible increased risk; it does not show that cardiovascular risk is eliminated.
survodutide.safety: Gastrointestinal adverse events led to discontinuation in 19.3% and 20.8% of the survodutide groups versus 1.9% with placebo. Serious adverse-event rates were similar across groups.

cagrisema.findings: November 14, 2026: REDEFINE 9 randomized 309 adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes. At 68 weeks, the efficacy-estimand weight changes in two combination groups were −20.7% and −21.0%, versus −2.0% with pooled placebo. Novo Nordisk funded the trial.
cagrisema.limits: The efficacy estimand addresses a hypothetical treatment-adherence scenario and is not interchangeable with treatment-regimen estimates. This placebo-controlled study does not establish superiority between the two studied combination regimens or validate custom blends.
cagrisema.safety: Adverse events were reported in 99% and 95% of treated participants in the combination groups versus 91% with placebo; most were mild or moderate and gastrointestinal-related. Small trial size and no reported deaths do not establish long-term safety.

tirzepatide.findings: November 9, 2026: In a 40-week randomized study, 120 adults receiving tirzepatide were assigned to resistance exercise or usual activities. The exercise group lost less total lean soft tissue: between-group difference 1.09 kg (95% CI 0.43–1.75). Measured strength improved with exercise while declining in the comparison group.
tirzepatide.limits: Both groups lost lean soft tissue; the finding is not complete muscle preservation. Lean-tissue measurements and muscle function are distinct outcomes. This study does not establish the effects of adding another peptide.

semaglutide.findings: November 11, 2026: A prespecified secondary SOUL analysis of 9,650 high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes reported fewer total first and subsequent major cardiovascular events with oral semaglutide: 683 versus 791 with placebo (mean ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.76–0.97). This is another analysis of the same trial population. Separately, a November 8 randomized mechanistic study in 81 adults with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction found lower exercise cardiac filling pressure after 52 weeks.
semaglutide.limits: SOUL concerns an oral formulation and a high-risk diabetes population; it cannot be generalized to every formulation or lower-risk population. The 81-person heart-failure study measured hemodynamics, not mortality. Multiple analyses of the same trial are not independent replications.
semaglutide.safety: SOUL reported treatment discontinuation for adverse events in 15.5% with oral semaglutide versus 11.6% with placebo. The November COURAGE phase 2 trial studied experimental antibodies with semaglutide; the triple-treatment group had unfavorable safety and tolerability despite improved body-composition measures. This does not validate research-peptide combinations.

regulatory_sources.decision: Add state-authority distinction; policy is not approval or final bulks-list addition.

bpc-157.text: A production-method study examined BPC-157 fusion proteins expressed in bacteria and tested gastric injury in rats. This is preclinical work on specific fusion constructs, not a controlled human trial or evidence of equivalent activity for other BPC-157 preparations.

ghk-cu.text: A 2026 tissue-engineering study attached GHK-Cu to polymer microspheres and reported mineralization and vessel-formation signals in laboratory assays. These scaffold results do not establish human skin rejuvenation, bone healing, or the effects of injected free GHK-Cu.

mots-c.text: A pilot study in 32 peritoneal-dialysis patients measured endogenous MOTS-c in several body fluids and reported associations with oxidative-stress and vascular measures. Participants were not tested in a trial of administered MOTS-c. Such associations cannot establish that supplementation improves vascular health or exercise performance.

thymosin-a1.text: A single-centre retrospective cohort of 327 critically ill adults with tuberculosis-related sepsis found an association between thymosin alpha-1 exposure and lower observed 28-day mortality after statistical adjustment. This was not randomized; confounding and treatment-selection effects prevent a causal treatment-benefit conclusion. It does not establish general immune enhancement.
